title: Nissan UK launches first ‘real-world’ driverless pilot
source_used: WardsAuto (its article reports Nissan's release of 28 Sep 2026)
key_facts: Nissan UK's business unit will bring autonomous driving services to Cambridge to test its latest technology in an urban environment.
The pilot, called ADventure, will be coordinated by the automaker, local authorities, commuters and residents; the company's release is dated 28 Sep.
It uses a specially adapted 2022 Nissan Leaf electric vehicle.
The pilot is part of a government-funded research project that launched in September 2023 at the University of Warwick.
Nissan Technical Center Europe leads the project, and the goal is a blueprint to roll out in other communities.
The example given is older people who do not drive and must travel to medical appointments.
quote_evidence: Nissan U.K.’s business unit will bring autonomous driving services to the university city of Cambridge and test its latest technology in an urban enviorment and create a blueprint to launch in other communities.
The pilot trial, dubbed “ADventure,” will be coordinated between the automaker, local authorities, commuters and residents, the company said in its Sept. 28 release.
why_it_matters_hint: A self-driving pilot for people who cannot drive, if it runs; the news itself is older.
